title: Orchestrated access SLA classifier and customer intake for admin requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and platform teams open a high volume of non-bug admin/access requests (RBAC role creation, SSO/SAML enablement, SCIM provisioning config, org policy exceptions). Current triage is manual, inconsistent across regions, and often routed to the wrong team tier which causes SLA miss and poor developer experience.

Goal: Build an orchestrated intake + classifier that automatically assigns requests to the correct SLA tier and routing path based on request attributes (customer size, data sensitivity, requested change type, deployment mode: hosted/dedicated/private). The system should reduce manual handoffs by 50%, surface a clear SLA and estimated delivery window to the customer, and provide telemetry for continuous improvements.

Scope: Design the intake form fields and decision lattice; implement an initial rule-based classifier backed by mapping tables for RBAC/SSO/SCIM patterns; connect to the Service Routing layer to auto-assign to Enterprise Ops or Solutions Engineering; add audit logging and tagging for Closed-loop metrics. Include UI copy in Console for visible SLA and expected next steps.

Out of scope: Full ML intent classifier (phase 2), automated change execution workflows (will create separate ENG tickets), billing/chargeback automation.

Success metrics: 50% reduction in manual reassignment within 8 weeks of launch; median time-to-acknowledge <= 4 business hours for P1 admin intake; 80% of requests correctly routed by rule-based classifier measured against human-reviewed ground truth.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form in Console for admin/access requests with fields: customer org size, requested action (RBAC/SSO/SCIM/policy), environment (hosted/dedicated/private), data sensitivity, urgency, contact info, supporting docs link
Rule-based classifier maps >= 80% of historical customer requests to a target queue (Enterprise Ops / Solutions Eng / Platform) in a test data set
Auto-assignment to the correct Linear queue with SLA tag and visible ETA in the Console UI
Audit log entries created for each intake and stored for 90 days with request metadata
Dashboard: counts by route, accuracy vs human review, median time-to-acknowledge, reassignment rate
notes: Trade-offs: Starting with a deterministic rule table increases predictability and makes audits easier; however it may underfit new phrasing — plan for iterative updates and metrics-driven expansion to an ML-backed intent model in Q3.
Privacy: For private/VPC customers, intake metadata must avoid exporting sensitive config details; store identifiers and hashed context where possible.
Routing granularity: Initial plan uses 3 queues (Enterprise Ops, Solutions Eng, Platform). Future stratification may add a 'Dedicated Oncall' queue for P0 infra emergencies.
RBAC templates: We will include a library of suggested role templates to reduce churn; these templates should be authored by PLAT and validated by Security.
SAML/SCIM workstreams: SCIM provisioning often requires customer IdP coordination — add an optional 'technical onboarding' checkbox to route to onboarding docs + Solutions Eng.
Dependency on ENG-12455 (routing service mutex changes) and PM-9951 (structured-intake for org security requests) for schema compatibility.
